Section B
Answer any three questions.
Each question is introduced by stimulus material. In your answers you may refer to the material and/or
other examples you have studied.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify two benefits people may gain from a good education.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain two reasons for a change in the amount of tax revenue a government receives.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Analyse the economies of scale a school may gain from an increase in its size.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss whether or not having a high proportion of a country’s population over the age of 64
is a benefit to its economy.

text: Since 2016, South Korea’s population has declined, due to a falling birth rate, and a high proportion
of its population is now aged over 64. The South Korean government has used tax revenue to give
cash incentives to couples to have more children. However, many parents have chosen to have
fewer children and spend more on each child to ensure they get a good education. South Korea
now has fewer but larger schools.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define external growth of firms.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain two reasons why low-skilled workers may be highly paid.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Analyse how fiscal policy can increase employment.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Discuss whether or not a government should provide free fruit to consumers.

text: Some firms in Monaco have experienced external growth. Firms in Monaco pay high wages.
Workers in Monaco benefit from fiscal policy which contributes to high employment. Their
government does impose VAT on food, including fruit. Some economists have suggested that
instead of taxing fruit, governments should provide free fruit to consumers.

parts.text: Define a shortage.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain two ways a firm can increase its profit.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Analyse the reasons why the price elasticity of demand for one brand of luxury chocolates is
likely to be different from that of salt.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Discuss whether or not a country should import most of the food it consumes.

text: In 2021, the Suez Canal was blocked by one of the world’s biggest container ships. This affected
some firms’ profits and caused a shortage in a number of products. The delivery of luxury chocolate
and salt, for example, was delayed. These two goods have differences in their price elasticity
of demand. The disruption to international trade created particular difficulties for those countries
which import most of the food they consume.

text: New Zealand is a high-income country with a low unemployment rate and a surplus of imports
over exports. Recently, its government has made some important economic decisions. In 2022,
it banned everyone born after 2008 from buying cigarettes. A year before, it gave permission for
firms to explore for oil in the country.
